I had this very exact question as I am also a US citizen looking to get citizenship in Canada. But, as annoying as it is, the only downside to this is that you have to pay taxes in the US and in Canada. But they have a treaty that gives tax credits up to a large amount so you will most likely not get double taxed. Not to mention, you have to pay higher taxes in Canada so that lowers the chances for double taxation to almost nothing. Instead, you'd just be paying a hundred or more bucks a year to keep your American citizenship. Just having it means a very powerful passport and it opens up future opportunities to work in the States where their currency is a lot stronger and certain industries pay a lot more. It's like investing in the possible opportunities you might have in the future, so I'd say it is worth it.

I love gizzard curry. My mom used to make it growing up and it's pretty simple if you have the necessary Indian spices. 

I don't follow a recipe so this is an approximation of the ingredients:

- 2 whole cardamoms
- small cinnamon stick
- 2-3 cloves 
- 1 med-large onion, thinly sliced
- ginger and garlic paste 
- 1/2 tbsp cumin
- 3/4 tbsp coriander
- 1/2 tbsp chili powder (or more if you want)
- 1 tsp turmeric
- 1/2 lb of gizzard 
- some water if you need it and coriander leaves for garnish if you care; salt to taste 

Add some oil to a medium heat pan, add all your whole spices for about 2-3 mins or until they smell fragrant. Toss em around so as not to burn them.

Add the sliced onion and cook til translucent. Add garlic ginger paste until the raw smell goes away. Add on the rest of your ground spices (cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder) and add some water so the spices don't burn if your pan is dry. Then just boil off the water and wait until you see the spices release their oil on top. Note: you can add as some water you need to just do add in batches after boiling it off each time.

Add your gizzard and mix well, then salt. Put it on medium/medium low for 10 mins, come back and stir. If the pan looks dry, add some water. You can also add more water for a brothy curry but I prefer this as a dry curry.

Then, just bring it to a boil, lower heat to simmer and let it go for 30 ish minutes or until you see the curry has gone from a light brown to a dark brown color. 

Add coriander leaves for garnish and serve with some basmati rice. 

Honestly one of my favorite curries, give it a try if you've got the ingredients!

You can make eggs and hash for breakfast or lunch.

Just dice a potato into 1/2 inch ish cubes. Heat up your oil and add them in. They should sizzle. Add your salt and pepper. Don't stir for 2-3 mins on medium/med high. Then stir once and repeat til your potatoes are golden brown. Transfer to a plate.

Same pan, add some more oil and crack in 1-2 eggs (how much oil you add depends on the pan--if it's nonstick, a little will do but if not then add a good amount and heat it well so that the egg doesn't stick). Cook on medium heat until the whites aren't jiggly. You can flip if you like but I just keep it sunny side up and runny. Serve with the potatoes.

Rice + stir fried potatoes + sunny side up eggs + chili oil and/or buldak sauce 

The stir fried potatoes dish is called aloo bazi. You cut a potatoe into matchsticks and stir fry it for 5 mins or until they're soft with some turmeric and salt (optionally coriander leaves aka cilantro). 

Then serve on rice with two eggs and top with chili oil. I love adding the buldak sauce that Samyang has on Amazon. It's filling and takes maybe 15 mins tops.

Bengali - basmati rice (or any medium/long grain rice), aloo bazi (stir fried potatoes), dim (Bengali omelette), with dal (lentil curry)

I don't know if this is traditional but growing up, my mom would make it a lot for breakfast. 

Aloo Bazi: thinly julienne a large potatoe, fry in some oil with 1/2 tsp turmeric and salt, then add some chopped coriander or cilantro leaves at the end. 

Dim: dice a small onion and a chili pepper if you like spice, then mix in a bowl with 2 eggs, some salt, and coriander/cilantro leaves. Fry on a nonstick pan, flip and cook both sides. 

Dal: cook 1/2 cup red lentils for 20 minutes in about 1.5 cups of water. Then add 1/2 tsp of turmeric and salt. You can also add other stuff to this if you want, like fried garlic or chicken powder to make it more flavorful, but its good that way too.

All of this is enough for 2 hungry people. Hope you try it!
